[{"tag":"v1.2.2","date":"2026-09-23","name":"TensorCash 1.2.2","body":"# TensorCash 1.2.2 — staged Quick verification and SGLang mining support

TensorCash 1.2.2 introduces an exact fast path for CPU Quick verification,
experimental SGLang mining support, and security and reliability fixes across
the verifier, node and cosign bridge.

- **Staged Quick verification.** Avoids expensive collision aggregation when
  an exact certificate proves it unnecessary, with full verification of the
  remaining Quick checks and automatic fallback to the complete calculation.
  The optimization preserves existing verification decisions and pricing;
  the consensus kernel remains v6. Quick verification remains preliminary
  and does not replace model Full verification.
- **SGLang mining integration.** Adds the Apache-2.0 TensorCash PoW plugin for
  stock SGLang v0.5.18, miner-proxy routing and independent request identifiers
  for retries. Ordinary requests retain SGLang's stock sampling path. CPU
  contract and upstream compatibility checks passed, as did Docker builds
  for AMD64 and ARM64.
- **Correct chain context.** Batch triage and calibration use each share's
  own chain context. Detector activation follows the node's ruleset.
- **Security hardening.** Prevents execution of model-repository code during
  verifier model loading, authenticates cosign responses against the proposal
  issuer, and adds node resource bounds and sole-model replay protection.
- **Recovery and build fixes.** Restores relay reconnection after send failures,
  allows cosign response"},{"tag":"v1.2.1","date":"2026-09-20","name":"1.2.1","body":"# 1.2.1

- Adds the sealed Full-verification detector bundle.

Install both archives. Rebuild and update workers and gateway together.
Verify the files against `SHA256SUMS`.
"},{"tag":"pool-verify-pack-1.2.0d","date":"2026-09-19","name":"Verifier 1.2.0d and pool verification pack — candidate","body":"Verifier 1.2.0d and pool verification pack — candidate

Mode-V4 proofs under ruleset 4 now pass the shared prompt-scaffold and flat-region admission checks. Mainnet activation is candidate height 27615. The C++ Quick verifier and Python Quick/Full paths use the same integer predicates and shared vectors. Pre-sunset rules remain unchanged.

Full verification now skips the unused two-edge residual computation for v3 proofs. The final v3 verdict continues to use its upper-edge statistic. The native FlatBuffers unpacker rejects a BlockValidation without pow_blob instead of crashing.

The pool gateway preserves evidence rows during conversion and rejects unavailable evidence types. Admission probes fail closed when their files are absent and discover files added later. The converter corrections cover native installations; the Docker gateway already used the canonical converter.

Validation includes all 263 bcore unit suites, 182 native sunset tests, 21 Python sunset-path tests, and 20 pfunpack regressions. Source mirrors and shared vectors are checked for equality. The pack was independently rebuilt from the published TensorCash and bcore commits and the pinned gateway source; its tree and both archives reproduce exactly.

This scoped candidate tag identifies the verifier and pool pack. The existing node release tag is preserved.

Extract both archives into the same directory. Verify their hashes against RELEASE_SHA256SUMS before building. See SUNSET_ADMISSION.md and RELEASE_VALID"},{"tag":"pool-verify-pack-1.2.0c","date":"2026-09-16","name":"Verifier 1.2.0c and pool verification pack — candidate","body":"## Verifier 1.2.0c and pool verification pack

Full verification now checks support consistency for mode-V4 proofs using the existing replay candidates and the canonical active sampler support. Participating canaries count toward support. Missing or invalid replay evidence produces an explicit abstention. The new rule does not apply to v3 or legacy proofs, and the established rank-null calculation is retained.

This update packages the v3 compatibility fixes already on this branch: the `1e-4` sampling tolerance in scalar, vectorised and canonical-kernel paths; the original upper-edge Full probability statistic; and conversion of CUDA values to host values before NumPy credit checks. The verifier and pool package report `1.2.0c` / `proof-v4-support-v3-compat`, with an updated verdict-cache revision.

### Advisory integration

The advisory neural-scoring runtime is included. It uses a bounded background CPU process and the verifier's existing replay evidence. Scores, timeouts and unavailable inputs cannot alter authoritative verdicts. Bundle checks pin file hashes and require tensors-only weights; container builds fetch LFS objects and validate available bundles. No model weights are selected or enabled in this candidate. The final compatible model bundle will be added separately.

### Pool package

The standalone gateway and CPU/GPU worker package uses the same verifier source. Deployment examples use mainnet **X=26825, Y=26950, Z=27615**. The existing request-context cache is"},{"tag":"v1.2.0b","date":"2026-09-15","name":"TensorCash v1.2.0b","body":"TensorCash v1.2.0b restores the original v3 sampling tolerance and starts a fresh Quick/Smell validation cache.

- Restore the v3 inverse-CDF u band to `ATOL=1e-4`, including after X and Y. The support-membership, chosen-probability binding and length checks retain their existing activation. The exact v4 Gumbel race is unchanged.

- Move Quick/Smell verdicts to **cache epoch 3**. On the first upgraded start with an earlier cache present, the existing migration ignores old verdicts and resets block-index failure marks once. Affected blocks are then revalidated normally; invalid blocks must still fail.

This is a node compatibility hotfix over v1.2.0a. No additional proof-validity checks are relaxed. Full-verdict storage is unchanged.

Source review, public identity checks and Python syntax checks are complete. Compiled regression suites have not been run for this hotfix. "},{"tag":"v1.2.0a","date":"2026-09-14","name":"TensorCash v1.2.0a","body":"TensorCash v1.2.0a fixes verifier and miner issues found after v1.2.0.

- Fix GPU verification of v3 proofs during the Y-to-Z pricing window by reading replay membership inputs on the host.
- Apply the native anti-parrot gate before miner submission on both the C++ and vLLM classification paths, with counters for priced-gate outcomes.
- Fix package imports for the v4 pricing module and report `1.2.0a` in the verifier runtime identity.
- Include the post-v1.2.0 build and test corrections: complete standalone llama native build inputs, self-contained E2E mocks, corrected VDF/vLLM fixtures, and release publication fixes.

Mainnet activation remains X=26825, Y=26925, Z=27615. Proof-history reuse rejection remains v4-only. This release retains the existing bcore pin; the separate reindex and initial-sync fixes are not included.

"},{"tag":"v1.2.0","date":"2026-09-14","name":"TensorCash v1.2.0","body":"TensorCash v1.2.0 introduces proof v4 verification and miner checks for the coordinated mainnet transition.

**Binary builds are in progress. No downloadable binaries have been validated for this release yet.** Source archives are available from the tag; platform assets will follow successful build and validation.

### Mainnet activation

| Transition | Height | Behavior |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| X | 26825 | Proof v4 admission and proof-history collection begin. |
| Y | 26925 | V3 penalty pricing begins; proof-history reuse rejection applies to v4 candidates only. |
| Z | 27615 | V3 proofs are no longer admitted. |

Upgrade before height **26825**. Activation follows block height, not a fixed calendar time.

### Included changes

- Canonical Gumbel replay, native credit calculation, structure and candidate-band checks, and priced block-target verification.
- Native anti-parrot checks and validity checks using trusted request context. Block requests without trusted height preserve their preceding behavior.
- `enforce-requested` verifier mode for mixed fleets: explicitly requested new rulesets receive strict verification while legacy requests retain their replay behavior. Infrastructure failures produce no verdict rather than an invalid-proof verdict.
- Proof-history reuse rejection restricted to **v4 candidates**, with history collection retained across proof versions.
- Miner proxy anti-parrot and pricing checks, direct pre-send checks, and job-height propagation through the s"},{"tag":"v1.1.4c","date":"2026-09-07","name":"TensorCash v1.1.4c","body":"## v1.1.4c — same node code as v1.1.4b, complete build set

v1.1.4b's Windows desktop packages could not be built (a build-script issue on the release runners). v1.1.4c ships the identical node code with:

- the Windows packaging script fixed so it no longer appends a duplicate cargo linker table on persistent runners;
- the corrected functional test for the quick-cache epoch migration (the test mined on a node configured to reject its own blocks; the node code it covers is unchanged).

If you already run v1.1.4b, there is nothing to upgrade. See the v1.1.4b notes for the wallet/node fix: stale quick-verification verdicts no longer wedge a node, and the block-index failure marks they left behind are cleared on the first start of the new cache epoch.

No consensus changes. Release binaries and images appear here as the workflows complete."},{"tag":"v1.1.4b","date":"2026-09-07","name":"TensorCash v1.1.4b","body":"## Wallet/node fix: stale quick-verification verdicts no longer wedge a node

Some v1.1.4a nodes stopped following the chain after upgrading: a Quick/Smell verdict cached by the previous binary had rejected a block that the current verifier accepts, and the block index kept the failure mark, so every later block was refused.

- The persistent quick-verdict cache is now versioned (`blockvalidationdb_quick-v2`). Verdicts written by an earlier verifier are not consulted again; the old directory is left in place so a rollback still finds its own cache.
- On the first start of the new cache epoch the node clears the block-index failure marks left by those stale verdicts (the same operation as `reconsiderblock`), re-validates the affected blocks, and only then records completion. An interrupted first start repeats the step. Genuinely invalid blocks fail again and stay rejected.
- No manual `reconsiderblock` or cache deletion is needed. A node that is still stuck after upgrading can still use `revalidateblock <hash>` / `reconsiderblock <hash>`.

Build: the cosign-bridge images and workflows now build with Rust 1.98 (newer transitive crates require rustc 1.88).

No consensus changes. Release binaries and images appear here as the workflows complete."},{"tag":"v1.1.4a","date":"2026-09-01","name":"v1.1.4a — StepBind step-nonce binding","body":"## v1.1.4a — StepBind step-nonce binding (consensus)

Follow-up to **v1.1.4**. Activates **StepBind**: a prompt-bound effective step nonce
that closes the residual per-step grinding surface in proof-of-inference.

### What changed
- **StepBind activation** — mainnet activation at height **24870**. Each
  proof-of-inference step, and the final proof hash, now incorporate an *effective
  step nonce* `E = H(tag | prompt_commitment | present | admission_nonce)` in place
  of the raw nonce. Because `E` is derived from the whole prompt commitment, any
  change to the prompt — including model-invisible tokens (duplicate-embedding,
  special, or out-of-window ids) — re-derives `E` and invalidates every step at
  once. This removes the "re-aim reused evidence" surface that remained after the
  pad-slot fix, at no additional cost to honest miners.
- **Grace window** to **2026-09-08 23:59:59 UTC** — flagless short-prompt legacy
  proofs stay valid through the cutoff, so miners can upgrade without interruption.
- **`ZMQ_ASSUME_STEPBIND` deployment flag** for the direct node→miner job path. The
  work-unit path signals StepBind explicitly; the direct path defaults to legacy
  unless this flag is set. Off by default.

### Operator action
- Consensus change: block producers must run **v1.1.4a or later before height 24870**.
  Miner images are being updated; pool operators will advise when available.
"},{"tag":"v1.1.4","date":"2026-08-31","name":"v1.1.4 — Pad-slot zero binding","body":"## v1.1.4 — Pad-slot zero binding (consensus)

Consensus hardening for the proof-of-inference prompt commitment.

### What changed
- **Pad-slot zero enforcement** — mainnet activation at height **24735**. Masked
  prompt positions are now bound to token id `0`. This closes a proof-forgery
  surface where masked prompt slots could be varied without changing the prompt
  commitment ("pad-slot grinding"), by forcing every masked slot to a single
  canonical value at and after the activation height.
- **Supporting proof-admission fixes** carried forward from the testnet line,
  tightening the checks applied when a proof is admitted.

### Operator action
- This is a consensus change: run **v1.1.4 or later before height 24735** to stay on
  the canonical chain. Superseded by the StepBind activation in **v1.1.4a**
  (height 24870) — run the latest release.
"},{"tag":"v1.1.3","date":"2026-08-30","name":"TensorCash v1.1.3","body":"## Miner: global VDF fallback

Consensus verifies a block's VDF purely against `hashPrevBlock`, so one (tick, proof) pair per parent is valid in every block built on that parent. The explorer now publishes such a checkpoint at `https://mempool.tensorcash.org/api/v1/vdf` (and `/api/v1/vdf/<hashPrevBlock>`).

The miner proxy fetches it on every block change (and every 2 s), **verifies it locally with `chiavdf.verify_from_hash`** — the same check consensus runs — and injects it whenever it leads the tick it already holds by at least one checkpoint. The local prover keeps running and takes over again once it overtakes; whichever tick is higher wins. Nothing from the explorer is ever trusted blindly: a failed verification is counted in `/status → vdf.remote_fallback.rejected` and dropped.

- On by default. `VDF_FALLBACK_ENABLED=false` disables it; `VDF_FALLBACK_URL` points it at another explorer.
- Without chiavdf there is nothing to verify with, so the fallback stays off unless `VDF_FALLBACK_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED=true` is set explicitly.
- `LockFreeContext.update_vdf` is now per-block monotonic and block-guarded; the snapshot records `vdf_source` (`local`/`remote`).
- The seeder image builds the chiavdf wheel.

No consensus changes."},{"tag":"v1.1.2a","date":"2026-08-27","name":"TensorCash v1.1.2a","body":"# TensorCash v1.1.2a

## Mainnet upgrade for block producers

v1.1.2a supersedes the withdrawn v1.1.2 release and corrects its production proof-evidence validation.

- **Activation:** mainnet height **24150**
- **Testnet:** unchanged
- **Scope:** bcore update for block producers and consensus-validating nodes
- **History:** forward-only; existing blocks are unaffected

If you installed v1.1.2, replace it with v1.1.2a before activation. An outdated block producer may create a block that upgraded nodes reject.

## Included changes

- Soft-fork tightening of accepted proof-of-inference proofs to disincentivise prompt engineering and degenerate entropy profiles
- Stale-verdict rollback protection
- Batched mining work-unit issuance
- Numeric RPC support for batch work units
- Mining-RPC safety guard
- Hotfix ensuring production proof evidence is handled correctly and required on every applicable block-acceptance path

Applied retrospectively for measurement, approximately 0.25% of historical proofs would not satisfy the tightened requirements.

## Required revisions

- TensorCash: `9bdeb44d76ef93f24f42b88c78cf1ed3402594f4`
- bcore: `8483a19095cef56203bd21d8e8aebbba9d98bb6f`

Release binaries and images will appear here as the public builds complete.

## Acknowledgements

Thanks to [The AllFather](https://x.com/t_allfather) ([GitHub](https://github.com/t-allfather)) for independently offering advice and input on the entropy-binding solutions."},{"tag":"v1.1.1","date":"2026-08-18","name":"v1.1.1","body":""},{"tag":"v1.1.0a","date":"2026-08-03","name":"TensorCash v1.1.0a — Windows-Compatible Build","body":"# TensorCash v1.1.0a

- Pinned bcore commit: `4"},{"tag":"v1.1.0","date":"2026-08-03","name":"TensorCash v1.1.0 — Mandatory Mainnet Upgrade","body":"# TensorCash v1.1.0

**Mandatory mainnet upgrade — update before block 20,440.**

Miners, full nodes, explorers, and verification services running an earlier release will diverge from the upgraded network when block 20,440 activates. The block height—not an estimated time—is authoritative.

## What changes

This release replaces the legacy 2,016-block difficulty adjustment with ASERT. Difficulty is recalculated after every block, allowing the network to respond progressively as mining capacity changes while retaining the 10-minute target block interval.

At activation, the network applies a one-time easier difficulty reset. Blocks may arrive faster initially while ASERT moves the network toward its target cadence.

It also includes validation-liveness recovery, asset live-supply-cap and ICU governance updates, bulletin-board relay routing, cross-chain HTLC work, miner and verification service updates, and the shared-validation-service TIP documents.

## Activation schedule

| Phase | Height | Behaviour |
|---|---:|---|
| Activation | **20,440** | One-time reset to `nBits 0x1e0597a7` |
| Initial response | 20,441–46,737 | ASERT with a 12-hour half-life |
| Long-run phase | **46,738 onward** | Fresh anchor and 48-hour half-life |
| Review point | 120,440 | Operational review only; no automatic consensus change |
